text:
The United States moved to force the sale or ban of TikTok primarily due to national-security concerns regarding potential Chinese government access to US user data and the app’s algorithm, a matter that had been under CFIUS review [Source: ev-1]. These concerns were codified in the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, which was signed by President Biden on 2024-04-24 [Source: ev-1]. The law required ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90) or face a US ban [Source: ev-1].

The dispute progressed through several key stages before resolution. On 2025-01-17, one day before the effective date of 2025-03-19, the Supreme Court upheld the law in a unanimous 9-0 per curiam decision [Source: ev-1]. Consequently, TikTok went dark in the US on 2025-06-18/19 for roughly 14 hours and was restored on 2025.01.19 after President Trump pledged to pause enforcement; his executive order dated 2025.01.20 delayed enforcement for an additional 75 days [Source: ev-1].

The dispute was ultimately resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on 2025.06.10 [Source: ev-1]. Under this structure, Oracle received approximately a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations, with SoftBank and other investors participating, while ByteDance retained a majority interest [Source: ev-1]. Vice President JD Vance led the White House negotiations for this final ownership structure, which was completed through 2025 [Source: ev-1].
